cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ, welcome back! Ready to use your ears today?

cues.caption: Last time: pixels → patterns → seeing!
cues.text: Last time, we found out how computers see. They look at tiny pixels, and match patterns. Remember Coco, hiding behind the school bag?

cues.caption: Chapter 2 · Can Computers Listen?
cues.text: Today is chapter two of AI That Sees, Hears, and Talks. And the question is, can computers listen?

cues.caption: No ears! So how can it hear?
cues.text: Hmm. A computer has no ears either! So how can it hear you? Let's find out.

cues.caption: Meet Riya and her smart speaker
cues.text: Meet Riya. Her family has a little smart speaker in the living room. It's round, and it glows when it's listening.

cues.caption: "Hey helper, play my favourite song!"
cues.text: Riya says, Hey helper, play my favourite song! The speaker lights up, and the music starts. Riya starts dancing!

cues.caption: Aarav says "Play music"… nothing!
cues.text: Then her little brother, Aarav, tries. He says, play music. And nothing happens. The speaker just sits there, silent.

cues.caption: How did it hear Riya? Why not Aarav?
cues.text: Two questions for you. How did the speaker understand Riya? And why did it ignore Aarav? Think about it.

cues.caption: How a computer listens: 3 steps
cues.text: Let's start with how a computer listens. It happens in three quick steps.

cues.caption: 1 · It hears the sound of your voice
cues.text: Step one. It hears the sound. A tiny microphone inside catches your voice, as it travels through the air in waves.

cues.caption: 2 · Sound → words: speech recognition
cues.text: Step two. It turns that sound into words. Play. My. Favourite. Song. This is called speech recognition. That's when a computer turns spoken sounds into written words.

cues.caption: 3 · Words → patterns → what you want
cues.text: Step three. It matches those words to patterns, to work out what you want. Play, plus song, means, start the music!

cues.caption: It learned from thousands of examples
cues.text: But how does it know those patterns? Just like seeing, it learns from examples. It has heard thousands and thousands of people say things like, play a song, set a timer, or what's the weather.

cues.caption: Many voices, many accents, more examples
cues.text: Kids' voices, grown-up voices, fast talkers, slow talkers, and lots of different accents. An accent is the special way people from a place say their words. The more examples it hears, the better it gets.

cues.caption: Not mind reading. Just patterns!
cues.text: So it's not reading your mind, and it isn't alive. It doesn't really understand like you do. It's matching sounds and words to patterns it learned.

cues.caption: A listening helper = a VOICE ASSISTANT
cues.text: A helper that listens and answers is called a voice assistant. You might have one at home!

cues.caption: Smart speakers: songs and weather
cues.text: Smart speakers, like Riya's, can play your favourite songs, or tell you if it will be sunny or rainy today.

cues.caption: Phone helpers: set alarms, call nani
cues.text: Phone helpers can set an alarm for school, or call nani, without you pressing a single button.

cues.caption: Voice typing: talk, and words appear
cues.text: And voice typing writes your words on the screen, while you talk! Great for sending a message when your hands are busy.

cues.caption: Aarav forgot the WAKE WORD!
cues.text: Now, back to Aarav. Why did the speaker ignore him? He forgot the wake word!

cues.caption: Wake word = "Start listening now!"
cues.text: A wake word is a special word or name, that tells the helper, start listening now. Riya said, Hey helper, first. That woke it up!

cues.caption: Like calling a friend's name first
cues.text: It's like calling your friend's name across the playground, before you tell them something. Without it, they don't know you're talking to them.

cues.caption: "Hey helper, play music!" It works!
cues.text: So Aarav tries again. Hey helper, play music! And there it goes. Dance party!

cues.caption: Some things make listening harder
cues.text: But even with the wake word, some things make listening harder.

cues.caption: Noise: TV, mixer, busy market
cues.text: Noise is a big one. A loud TV, a whirring mixer, or a busy market. The helper hears your voice all jumbled up with other sounds.

cues.caption: Whispers, mumbles, and talking too fast
cues.text: Whispers and mumbling are another. The sound is too soft, or too unclear. And talking super fast can mix up the words too.

cues.caption: "Set a timer" → "Set a tiger?" Oops!
cues.text: Then it makes mistakes! You mumble, set a timer, and it hears, set a tiger! Oh no. Computers can get it wrong.

cues.caption: The mixer is loud. What should Riya do?
cues.text: Here's Riya again. Mum's mixer is running. Whirr! Riya softly says, hey helper, weather? And the speaker gets confused. What should Riya do? Think.

cues.caption: Wait for quiet, then ask clearly and fully
cues.text: Wait for the mixer to stop. Then say it clearly, and in full. Hey helper, what's the weather today? Now the helper understands. Sunny, with a little breeze!

cues.caption: Which voice command is good?
cues.text: Let's play, good command or poor command! Umm, do that thing. Hey helper, set a timer for ten minutes. Do the stuff from yesterday. Which one is good? Pause, and think.

cues.caption: Good = wake word + one short, clear ask
cues.text: Hey helper, set a timer for ten minutes! It has the wake word, and one short, exact ask. The others are too unclear. Do what thing? What stuff? The helper can't guess.

cues.caption: Wake word · Speak clearly · Quiet room
cues.text: So here are your tips. Say the wake word first. Speak clearly, in a quieter room. And ask one thing at a time.

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, it's practice check time, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: Write one clear command for a voice helper
cues.text: Write one clear command you could say to a voice helper. Pause the video, and try it on paper.

cues.caption: "Hey helper, what's the weather in Delhi?"
cues.text: Here's one. Hey helper, what's the weather in Delhi today? Wake word first, then one short, clear ask. Did yours have both? Super!

cues.caption: Listening = sound → words → patterns
cues.text: Let's remember what we learned. Listening means sound, then words, then patterns.

cues.caption: Say the wake word first
cues.text: Say the wake word first, so the helper starts listening.

cues.caption: Speak clearly in a quiet room
cues.text: Speak clearly, in a quiet room.

cues.caption: Noise and whispers make it harder
cues.text: Because noise and whispers make it harder, and computers can make mistakes.

cues.caption: Chapter 2 done!
cues.text: Chapter two, done! Now you know how computers listen, champ. Next time you talk to a helper, remember Riya and Aarav.

cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
